title: Consistent metering for embeddings and structured tool executions (non-chat endpoints)
creator: Maya Chen
description: Investigate and implement a deterministic, auditable metering model for non-chat endpoints that invoke embeddings, rerank operations, and structured tool/function executions. Goal is to ensure customers are billed exactly once per logical operation even when we perform speculative prefetches, partial retries, or fall back across model variants.
background: We have recurring customer reports and internal audits showing inconsistent charges when a single user request triggers multiple internal steps (embeddings prefetch, reranker calls, tool function invocations that return structured outputs). Causes include speculative prefetch, retry logic on partial failures, non-idempotent billing keys, and mismatch between rate-limiter enforcement and metering increments. Existing tickets solved pieces (attribution reconciliation, partial-charge fixes) but customers still see duplicate or missing charges for complex non-chat workflows.
acceptance_criteria: API-level request ID or deterministic billing key is generated for every logical non-chat request that can span embeddings, rerank, and tool calls
Metering events emitted for a logical request sum to a single canonical charge in the billing ledger under normal success
In cases of speculative prefetch or prewarming, a configurable consumer-cost flag determines whether prefetch tokens are billed and this flag is surfaced in audit logs

Retries and partial-success scenarios (e.g., some tools succeed, others fail) result in predictable billing: successful sub-ops billed once, failed sub-ops billed according to current policy and clearly documented
Rate limiter and quota counters reflect canonical logical requests (not raw internal retries) to avoid accidental quota depletion
End-to-end trace linking metering events to request, route, model variant, and PR numbers for postmortem and customer disputes
technical_design: 1) Billing Key: Generate a canonical billing_key for each incoming non-chat request. billing_key is derived from stable inputs: customer_id, endpoint_id, request_unix_ts_rounded_to_1s, client_request_id if provided. This key is idempotent across retries within a 5-minute sliding window. 2) Metering Events: All internal sub-ops (embed call, rerank call, tool invocation) will emit metering events with billing_key and subop_type. The ledger will dedupe by billing_key+subop_type+sequence_index. 3) Speculative Prefetch Flag: Introduce metering metadata field consumer_billed: true/false. Prefetch operations default to consumer_billed=false unless customer config enables prefetch billing. 4) Partial Success Policy: When sub-ops partially succeed, bill only for successful sub-ops and emit a reconciliation marker event. 5) Rate Limiter Integration: Rate limiter will decrement quota using logical_request_tokens computed from canonical request fingerprint. Internal retries will not consume additional quota tokens if they are within the idempotency window and share the billing_key. 6) Observability: Add signal points in console (per-route metering dashboard) showing canonical vs raw metering, and surface per-request metering traces for disputes.
implementation_notes: Add billing_key generation in api-router service before fanout to embedding/rerank/toolchain
Patch each internal client (embed-service, reranker, tool-runner) to accept billing_key and consumer_billed flag and include them in metering events
Modify metering-collector to dedupe using billing_key+subop_type+seq_index and to honor consumer_billed metadata
Extend rate-limiter to accept canonical token units and to consult billing_key idempotency cache (redis) to prevent double-debits
Add migration for historical edge-case reconciliation: backfill reconciler to mark disputed invoices and generate corrective credits when duplicate billing is detected
Add feature flag 'canonical-billing-v1' gated for rollout and immediate rollback capability
testing_plan: Unit tests for billing_key deterministic derivation with/without client_request_id
Integration tests simulating speculative prefetch with consumer_billed=false ensure no customer charge
Chaos tests that trigger retries and partial failures to validate only intended sub-ops are billed
Quota tests verifying multiple internal retries do not consume additional quota within idempotency window
End-to-end test that exports metering events and validates ledger deduplication and invoice generation
Customer-simulated acceptance tests using a staging account with runway credits and a sample pipeline that does embeddings->rerank->toolchain
rollout_plan: Feature-flag gated canary rollout to 5% of traffic for non-enterprise customers
Monitor canonical_vs_raw_billing_ratio metric and customer dispute volume for 72 hours
Progressively increase traffic to 25% then 100% while watching cost delta and error budget
Open communication with enterprise customers and offer opt-in early access for teams that want prefetch billing
If issues detected, flip feature flag off, run reconciliation to fix any interim ledger inconsistencies
